name: search-morph
title: Search Morph
description: A search button that stretches into a search field, with Cancel sliding in and results rising beneath.

perf.budget: One shared value drives the stretch, the field and Cancel. The shell's edges animate, so it lays out for the length of the spring; nothing runs at rest.

measurements.notes: Measured with its own script (open, type, close) since the default gestures miss it; slower frames come from the keyboard opening and closing.

a11y.reducedMotion: The field opens and closes in place.
a11y.screenReader: A Search button that becomes a text field named by the placeholder, with Clear search and Cancel buttons. Hidden parts are hidden from screen readers.
a11y.touchTarget: The button, the clear button and the bar are all 48 pt tall.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { SearchMorph } from '@/components/kinetik/search-morph';

<SearchMorph value={query} onChangeText={setQuery} onSubmit={search} placeholder="Search places">
  <Results query={query} />
</SearchMorph>;
```

Give it the width it may grow into, for example `style={{ flex: 1 }}` in a header row. Closed, it sits at the end of that space as a 44 pt circle.

## When to use

- Headers where search is useful but should not take a full row until it is wanted.
- Lists and grids that filter as you type, with the results passed as children.

## When not to use

- Screens whose main job is search. Show the field open from the start.
- Desktop-style toolbars with room to spare. A plain field is easier to find.

## Notes

- The field takes focus a moment after it starts to open, so the keyboard does not race the morph.
- Cancel clears the text and closes. Control `open` with `onOpenChange` to hide a title while it is open, as the demo does.
- Children are rendered only while open, so results do not run their queries in the background.
- With reduced motion the field opens and closes in place.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add search-morph`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
